learning_outcomes.statement: The learner can define classes with __init__/self, distinguish instance from class attributes, and apply encapsulation and property to protect an object's state.

The learner can choose correctly between composition (HAS-A) and inheritance (IS-A), apply super()/method overriding, explain polymorphism and duck typing, and use dataclasses and special methods appropriately.

reviewers.attestation: Read scripts/build_chapter_14.py in full (all lesson-builder functions), cross-checked every printed/claimed code result by executing the corresponding snippets under the project's own .venv (Python 3.14.6), ran every canonical notebook for this chapter via scripts/run_notebook.py (under xvfb-run where the chapter uses turtle/tkinter), independently re-verified every grader's expected value, and confirmed the canonical source and review-surface sha256 values match the current committed state exactly.

criteria.rationale: Two factual defects were found and fixed during this batch: F-013 (MAJOR, 14-11) claimed a missing @radius.setter raises AttributeError when the code shown actually silently overwrites the property with no error at all; F-014 (MINOR, 14-23) had a truncated dataclass ValueError text. Every other claim across all 27 sections was independently re-executed under Python 3.14.6 and found correct.

Python-3.14-specific behaviors (exact TypeError/AttributeError text for self-binding and __init__ mistakes, dataclass field validation, __eq__/__hash__ interaction) verified against the actual installed 3.14.6 interpreter; the two defects above were themselves caught by this exact verification process.

self, инкапсуляция, композиция/наследование (HAS-A/IS-A), duck typing, специальные методы (not магические методы), dataclass all used precisely and consistently; six new terminology register entries added for this chapter's OOP vocabulary decisions.

The opener promises class/self/__init__, instance vs class attributes, encapsulation/property, composition, inheritance/super(), polymorphism/duck typing, special methods, dataclasses, and model-design judgment; full-chapter reading confirms every promised topic is delivered in the stated order.
This chapter has no random/reproducibility-dependent claims; not applicable beyond confirming its absence.
The opener states the chapter's scope (classes, self, encapsulation, composition/inheritance, polymorphism, special methods, dataclasses, design judgment) as concrete, checkable topics.
Assumes only Chapter 13's functions and the object model informally used since Chapter 6; every new term is introduced via an already-familiar object (turtle, string, list) before formal definition.
Opens with type(artist)/type('Python')/type([1,2,3]) -- objects the learner has used since Chapter 1 -- before any new class-definition syntax, consistent with the course's familiar-first pedagogy.

28 sections are chunked into clear sub-arcs (basics -> encapsulation/property -> composition -> inheritance/polymorphism -> special methods/dataclasses -> design judgment -> mini-projects) rather than one undifferentiated list.
14-26's Turtle race v2 mini-project closes the chapter with genuine transfer (a Gonka class composing multiple Uchastnik objects) rather than a topic recap.
Chapter 13's function-as-object model is explicitly and correctly reused for self/command callbacks; Chapter 11's aliasing concept is correctly reused for the mutable-class-attribute trap (14-08).

All internal cross-references (14-09's forward reference to 14-21's __eq__ fix, 14-15's forward reference to 14-16's super() fix) were checked and verified accurate once the referenced sections were themselves reviewed.

14-08 explicitly and correctly cross-references Chapter 13's mutable-default-argument trap as 'the same underlying principle' rather than silently repeating unrelated material -- verified this parallel is technically accurate.
Chapter number, title, and all 28 section identifiers match the PAGES navigation model and sidebar exactly.
